rv.q: If the show still works, it is largely because it boasts one of Lloyd Webber’s best, most tightly composed scores.
Yet those indestructibly fine songs — of which Don't Cry for Me Argentina isn't the best — wow us once more.

Kenwright and his co-director Bob Tomson have steeped themselves in this score and their polished account teases out nuggets of subtext at every turn, abetted on this occasion by the devastatingly good Eva of Madalena Alberto .
This revival itself is more escapism than decisive call to arms, but its high-voltage delivery ensures Eva's legend lives on.
For my part, it is the worst production of a musical I have ever seen on a West End stage.
A stunning revival of one of the greatest musicals of our time spearheaded by the gorgeous Madalena Alberto.
Treat yourself to a good seat near the front, ignore the underwhelming Marti Pellow, and you'll enjoy a classy evening of glittering musical theatre that deserves to be back in the West End.
But rather that these fine elements are battling against the starchy content and style, which feels dated and a little shabby.

cn.t: Lloyd Webber's classic score remains powerful, but this revival feels dated. Alberto's Eva impresses vocally while keeping emotional distance, though Pellow's Che disappoints and sound issues undermine Rice's sharp lyrics.
